mechanism: surface-fill.js algoCoverage()'s isMarkLaw() branch returned the hardcoded MK_ROW_COV=1/3 for every mark law. At the sparse end (masterPitch 5.8mm on a 40mm sphere at d=1) that keeps only 3 of the master grid's rulings as mark-law rows -- too few for any mark language to carry a sparse-but-complete texture. New markRowCoverage() (gated MK[TONE_ALGO].rowFloor, set ONLY on mkDashRamp's own MK entry) turns the constant into a FLOOR: clamp(masterPitch / (MK_ROW_TARGET_PEN * penWidth), MK_ROW_COV, 1), MK_ROW_TARGET_PEN=16 (4.8mm ceiling at a 0.3mm pen). solveAt()'s row-pitch divisor R and the diagnostic rowPitch publish both call the SAME markRowCoverage() so the scaffold and the tone solve never disagree. Structurally byte-identical wherever masterPitch/4.8 < 1/3 (measured: d>=50 on this fixture) because the clamp floor equals the old constant there.

byte_identity_arithmetic.d=1: masterPitch 5.816mm / 4.8mm = 1.212 -> clamped to 1 (max) -> 8-ish master rulings survive as rows instead of 3
byte_identity_arithmetic.d=50: masterPitch 1.501mm / 4.8mm = 0.3127 < 1/3=0.3333 -> clamps to MK_ROW_COV exactly -> byte-identical (verified: 73 marks pre and post on sphere, 79 on torus)
byte_identity_arithmetic.d=220: masterPitch ~0.35mm / 4.8mm = 0.073 -> clamps to MK_ROW_COV -> byte-identical (verified via scene3d-mkdashramp-dark-end.test.js, T4b's own floor, 4/4 unchanged)

byte_identity_sweep.coverage_as_fraction: MARK_LAWS lists 12 raw internal shapes; only 4 (mkDotScreen, mkTick, mkDashRamp, mkScribble) are members of the CURRENT Vectura.SCENE3D_TONE_LAWS roster, verified live. The other 8 (mkLozenge, mkChevron, mkComma, mkSFlick, mkCrossPlus, mkTriangle, mkDotLozenge, mkRadialFlick) are absent from both IDS and ALIASES -- unreachable via any styleTable, confirmed live (each fires 'unknown toneLaw ... falling back to ladder' and both trees resolve identically to plain ladder). Excluding them is not a coverage gap: comparing them would silently re-test 'ladder' eight times under a false label. fineLadder/phaseFineLadder are valid ALIASES into 'ladder' but the single-key clampStyleParam resolution used by this harness cannot set their sibling rungMode sub-param, so driving them here risks silently re-testing bare ladder under the alias's name -- excluded for the same disclosed reason.
